mirrors: agent-privacy-guard: benchmark/annotation.py (categories), benchmark/scoring.py (kind to category), core/category_policy.py (treatment)

categories.name: name
categories.covers: given name, family name or full name of a person

categories.name: email
categories.covers: any email address, generic mailboxes included

categories.name: phone
categories.covers: landline or mobile number, national or international

categories.name: address
categories.covers: street line with number and street, then postcode and city when they follow

categories.name: birth_date
categories.covers: a date the context marks as a date of birth

categories.name: banking
categories.covers: IBAN of any country, card number, card security code, bank account number

categories.name: secret
categories.covers: API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, the password inside a URL

trap_types.word_name: a given name used as an ordinary word or a place (Pierre the stone, Rose the colour, Paris the city)
trap_types.eponym: a person's name used for a thing: algorithm, law, unit, theorem (Dijkstra, Gauss, Levenshtein)
trap_types.library: a library, framework or tool that carries a name (Jackson, Flask, Pandas, Sphinx, Jinja)
trap_types.code_identifier: a variable, function, class or module name that contains a name (get_dupont_score, class Martin)
trap_types.company_name: a company named after a family name (Peugeot, Dupont Plomberie)
trap_types.email_lookalike: text shaped like an email that is not one (@app.route, @types/node, $USER@host)
trap_types.indicator_non_pii: a word that usually announces personal data or a secret, followed by a value that is not one (user=admin, TOKEN_TTL=3600, Bonjour à tous)
trap_types.placeholder: a stand-in where a secret would go (${DB_PASSWORD}, <password>, xxxx, ***, %(password)s)
